blocks.x: Health payers sit between clinical reality and administrative machinery: prior authorization, coding integrity, quality programs and member experience all hinge on reading clinical evidence quickly and acting on it consistently — at HIPAA-grade privacy. This page is the operating picture: what runs, what strains, and which capabilities move the numbers that decide the margin.

The work concentrates in prior authorization, claims coding integrity, quality/hedis reporting, with member service resolution close behind. Each of these paths produces data faster than decisions, and the gap between the two is where cost and risk accumulate.
In Health Insurance & Benefits, as operators describe it:

items: Requests bounce for missing clinical evidence that exists in notes; turn-around times breach SLAs and clinicians revolt.
Claims codes and clinical narratives never reconcile; coding integrity and HEDIS-style quality reporting both suffer.
Coverage decisions cite policies inconsistently; member appeals overturn on documentation that was never surfaced.
Payer PHI is premium breach inventory; third-party partners extend the surface.
Benefit questions span plans, networks and formularies; agents guess and complaints escalate.
Core claims systems bend slowly; benefit design changes take quarters.

blocks.x: Capability in Health Insurance & Benefits is not abstract: each domain lands as a named build on a named workflow. The patterns below are what we deploy there.

items: policy criteria mapped to chart evidence; submissions and appeals assembled
codes + narratives unified for coding integrity and quality reporting
coverage logic citing medical policy passages with provenance
classification-aware DLP, access analytics and BAA governance
